# m.options.unusual_trades

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Large trades and sweeps of US-listed options contracts, flagged by Massive.

Call it from a session `m`, made with `dm.MassiveSession()`:

```python
m.options.unusual_trades(symbols=None, *, start=None, end=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None, on_error=None)
```

- [Methods](README.md#query-methods): `fetch()`, `poll(interval)`
- Read from: REST
- `poll()` by default: `dm.PollMode.APPEND`, which appends each row it hasn't seen, identified by `Symbol`, `Timestamp` and `SequenceNumber`

[Dataset index](README.md)

## Arguments

A linked argument follows its rule under [shared arguments](README.md#shared-arguments) on the dataset index.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`symbols`](README.md#symbols) | Option contracts; leave it out for every contract. |
| [`start`](README.md#start) | The first instant, or the first day. |
| [`end`](README.md#end) | The instant after the last, or the last day. |
| [`sort`](README.md#sort) | Any of Massive's field names, such as `"size"`. Fields: any REST field under [Massive fields](#massive-fields). |
| [`order`](README.md#order) | The direction of `sort`. |
| [`limit`](README.md#limit) | The most rows to return, in total. A watchlist's `fetch()` caps every request instead. |
| [`filters`](README.md#filters) | Further endpoint parameters, such as `{"ticker_gte": "O:SPY"}`. Keys: `ticker_gt`, `ticker_gte`, `ticker_lt`, `ticker_lte`. |
| [`on_error`](README.md#on_error) | What a bad symbol or row does in this call (`dm.ErrorPolicy`). None, the default, takes each cause from the session's `MassiveConfig.on_error`. |

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The row's instrument, as Massive's ticker. From REST `ticker`: "The options ticker symbol (e.g., O:SPY260123C00687000)." |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the row, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the New York date of `Timestamp`. |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's event time. From REST `sip_timestamp`: "The nanosecond accuracy SIP Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the SIP received this trade from the exchange which produced it." |
| `OptionRoot` | String | The OCC root symbol of the contract (e.g., SPXW). Differs from the underlying for weekly roots and for contracts adjusted after a corporate action (e.g., AMCR1). |
| `Price` | double | The price of the trade. This is the price per share of the underlying, so the total dollar value of a trade is the price multiplied by the size and by the contract multiplier, which is typically 100 shares per contract. |
| `Size` | long | The size of a trade (also known as volume), in contracts. |
| `Conditions` | long[] | A list of condition codes. See Options Condition Codes (https://massive.com/docs/rest/options/market-operations/condition-codes) for what each code means. |
| `Exchange` | long | The exchange ID. See Exchanges (https://massive.com/docs/rest/options/market-operations/exchanges) for Massive's mapping of exchange IDs. |
| `Flags` | String[] | The unusual-activity cases the trade meets, as a list. Values: block_premium (notional premium of $100,000 or more), block_size (1,000 contracts or more), iso (intermarket sweep, condition 219). A trade that meets several cases carries every matching flag. |
| `SequenceNumber` | long | The sequence number represents the sequence in which trade events happened. These are increasing and unique per ticker symbol, but will not always be sequential. Values reset after each trading session/day. |
| `UnderlyingTicker` | String | The ticker of the contract's underlying (e.g., SPX). Weekly and adjusted roots are folded in, so SPXW contracts report SPX and AMCR1 contracts report AMCR; see root to tell them apart. It is Massive's text as sent, an index bare (`SPX`), so it is not the `Underlying` of the chain and the contracts, which writes an index as `I:SPX`. |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, by the local clock. Rows that arrive together share it. It isn't Massive's time, and later rows can carry earlier times. In a `poll()` table, it's the time of the poll the row's values came from. |
